== Biography ==

Flopsy is one of four young rabbits who live with their Mother in a sand-bank beneath the root of a great fir-tree. She is counted among the good little bunnies, marked by obedience and steady temperament in contrast to her brother Peter's willful nature.

When their Mother ventures into the wood to the baker's shop one morning, Flopsy, along with her siblings Mopsy and Cotton-tail, sets out down the lane to gather blackberries. This errand reflects the orderly habits encouraged by their Mother, who had warned all four rabbits against venturing into Mr. McGregor's garden. While Peter disobeys this instruction with grave consequences, Flopsy remains dutiful.

At day's end, after Peter returns home exhausted and unwell from his misadventure, Flopsy takes her supper with Mopsy and Cotton-tail, enjoying bread and milk together with the blackberries they had gathered. She represents the steady, obedient path set against Peter's reckless curiosity.

== Narrative role ==

Flopsy is one of four little rabbits born to Mrs. Rabbit, living with her siblings Mopsy, Cotton-tail, and [[Peter]] in a sand-bank beneath the root of a very large fir-tree. She is characterized as a good little bunny, a distinction that sets her apart from her naughty brother Peter.

When their mother sets out to the baker's shop one morning, Flopsy and her siblings Mopsy and Cotton-tail obey her instructions. Rather than venturing into the forbidden Mr. [[McGregor]]'s garden as Peter does, the three good little bunnies proceed down the lane to gather blackberries. While Peter suffers the consequences of his disobedience by eating stolen vegetables, becoming ill, and being put to bed with camomile tea, Flopsy and her sisters enjoy a wholesome supper of bread and milk with the blackberries they have collected.

== Personality ==

Flopsy is characterized by obedience and good behavior. She heeds her Mother's instructions and shows restraint where her brother Peter does not. When their Mother cautioned the young rabbits against entering Mr. McGregor's garden, Flopsy complied without question, choosing instead to gather blackberries down the lane alongside her siblings Mopsy and Cotton-tail. Her willingness to follow guidance stands in marked contrast to Peter's impulsive disobedience, revealing a temperament inclined toward propriety and caution.

Flopsy's virtue is rewarded with comfort and nourishment. While Peter suffered consequences for his transgression and was put to bed with medicinal camomile tea, Flopsy enjoyed a simple but wholesome supper of bread, milk, and the blackberries she had gathered. This distinction suggests that Flopsy's goodness is not merely praised but tangibly protected and sustained by her prudent choices.
